experiences.name: W Trek Multi-Day Hike
experiences.description: Embark on the iconic W Trek, a 4-5 day trekking route through Torres del Paine National Park covering the Valle del Francés, Grey Glacier, and the iconic Torres lookout. Experience dramatic landscapes of granite towers, turquoise lakes, and diverse Patagonian wildlife including guanacos and condors.
experiences.location: Torres del Paine National Park, Central Circuit

experiences.name: Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Trek to the base of the iconic three granite towers at sunrise for the most photographed view in Patagonia. The 8-hour round trip hike ascends through lenga beech forests and a steep moraine to reveal the breathtaking turquoise lagoon reflecting the towering peaks in golden morning light.
experiences.location: Sector Las Torres, Eastern Torres del Paine

experiences.name: Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition
experiences.description: Paddle through iceberg-dotted waters alongside the massive Grey Glacier, one of Patagonia's most spectacular ice fields. Guided kayaking tours bring you up close to towering blue ice walls and calving glaciers while navigating the pristine waters of Lago Grey surrounded by raw Patagonian wilderness.
experiences.location: Lago Grey, Western Torres del Paine

experiences.name: Valle del Francés Day Trek
experiences.description: Hike through the dramatic Valle del Francés, a glacially carved valley flanked by hanging glaciers, waterfalls, and the towering Paine Grande massif. The trail winds through native Patagonian forest to Mirador Británico, offering panoramic views of the central massif and surrounding peaks with frequent condor sightings overhead.
experiences.location: Valle del Francés, Central Torres del Paine

experiences.name: Puma and Wildlife Tracking Safari
experiences.description: Join an expert naturalist guide for a dawn wildlife tracking experience in the pampas and hillsides of Torres del Paine, one of the best places on Earth to spot wild pumas in their natural habitat. The guided 4x4 and on-foot excursion also offers sightings of guanacos, Andean foxes, rheas, and condors across the sweeping Patagonian steppe.
experiences.location: Laguna Amarga and Pampas Zone, Northern Torres del Paine

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Punta Arenas or Puerto Natales airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Collect luggage, arrange pre-booked budget transfer or shared shuttle to Puerto Natales (approx. 1.5-hour drive). Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and settle into your beachfront room. Grab a light snack if available at the accommodation.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or airport snack
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport food court
meals.dinner: Late-night snack from convenience store or hotel reception — pack some trail mix or instant noodles for arrival night to save costs

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book a shared shuttle from the airport to Puerto Natales to save money (approx. USD 10-15 vs USD 60+ for private taxi). Confirm check-in arrangements with Aegean Bliss Resort in advance given the late arrival. Pack a small overnight bag accessible during the flight for essentials.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a slow start, head to Puerto Natales town center on foot or by local bus. Visit the Costanera (waterfront promenade) along Última Esperanza Sound for stunning free views of mountains and sea. Explore the local market for budget supplies.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Museo Histórico Municipal de Puerto Natales (free or minimal entry fee) to learn about Patagonian history and culture. Stock up on trekking supplies, snacks, and groceries at local supermarkets (Unimarc or Lider) for the coming days in the park — this is your most important budget task of the day.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort. Organize and pack your gear for the days ahead. Plan your park entry and trail strategy using free maps available at the park office or downloaded offline.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared breakfast at accommodation or local panadería (bakery) — fresh bread, coffee, and jam for under USD 3
meals.lunch: Local almuerzo (set lunch menu) at a Puerto Natales restaurant — typically USD 6-9 for soup, main, and drink
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal using groceries purchased today — pasta with sauce is a classic budget trekker staple

day_by_day.notes: Buy a park entry pass for Torres del Paine online at the CONAF website (approx. USD 35 in high season for foreigners) to avoid queues. December is high season — trails and campsites are busy. Carry sufficient Chilean pesos as card acceptance is limited in the park.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure from Puerto Natales by budget public bus or shared transfer to Torres del Paine National Park (departs around 07:30, approx. USD 10-15 one way). Arrive at park entrance, show your CONAF pass, and collect trail maps. Head to the Laguna Amarga ranger station area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin an introductory hike to Laguna Amarga viewpoint — a relatively flat, accessible trail offering dramatic first views of the Torres granite towers and the surrounding steppe landscape. Spot Patagonian wildlife including guanacos, ñandús (rheas), and Andean condors soaring overhead.
day_by_day.evening: Set up camp at Camping Las Torres or Camping Chileno (budget campsite, approx. USD 10-18 per person) or return to Puerto Natales by afternoon bus if day-tripping. Enjoy the long Patagonian summer daylight (sunset around 22:00) with views of the towers turning golden.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared at accommodation before departure — oats, fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from groceries — sandwiches, nuts, dried fruit, and chocolate
meals.dinner: Camp stove meal at campsite — instant soup, dehydrated rice and beans, or pasta

day_by_day.notes: December days are very long in Patagonia with up to 17 hours of daylight — take advantage of this for flexible hiking schedules. Strong Patagonian winds are common in the afternoon; start hikes early. Carry at least 2 liters of water and a wind-proof jacket at all times.

day_by_day.morning: FEATURED EXPERIENCE — Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike: Wake at 04:00 and begin the iconic trek to the base of the three granite towers before sunrise. The trail from Camping Las Torres ascends through lenga beech forest, boulder fields, and a steep moraine to reach Laguna Torres at approximately 2,860m altitude. Total hike: 9km one way, 4-5 hours ascent.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at the mirador (viewpoint) at the base of the towers as the first golden light strikes the granite peaks — the most photographed moment in all of Patagonia. Spend time absorbing the view, taking photos, and having a well-earned snack. Begin the descent back to camp, arriving mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Rest tired legs at camp. Enjoy the long evening light with views of the surrounding landscape. Prepare a hearty camp dinner and share stories with fellow trekkers. Early bedtime to recover for the next day.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn energy snacks before the hike — energy bars, nuts, and instant coffee in a thermos
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at the base of the towers — sandwiches, fruit, chocolate, and hot tea from a thermos
meals.dinner: Substantial camp meal — instant mashed potatoes with tuna, hot soup, and crackers

day_by_day.notes: This is the highlight of the entire trip — do not miss it. Start no later than 04:30 to reach the towers at sunrise (around 06:00-06:30 in December). The final 45-minute ascent over the moraine is steep and requires careful footing. Dress in warm layers as temperatures at the top can be near freezing even in summer. Trekking poles are highly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning after the demanding towers hike. Take a leisurely walk around the Camping Las Torres area. Explore the nearby Río Ascencio valley floor on a flat, easy trail enjoying the beech forest and river sounds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike to Mirador Cóndor, a shorter viewpoint trail offering panoramic views of the Valle Ascencio and the eastern face of the Paine massif. Keep eyes on the sky for Andean condors with wingspans up to 3 meters riding thermal currents above the valley.
day_by_day.evening: Relocate camp or prepare for the next section of the trek. If continuing the W Trek, pack up and move toward Hotel Las Torres area. Alternatively, relax at camp and enjoy the spectacular evening alpenglow on the towers.

meals.breakfast: Slow breakfast at camp — oatmeal with dried fruit and nuts, instant coffee
meals.lunch: Camp lunch — crackers with peanut butter, cheese, and dried sausage
meals.dinner: Camp dinner — lentil soup with bread, hot chocolate

day_by_day.notes: Your body will need recovery time after the towers hike. This is intentionally a lighter day. Stay hydrated — the dry Patagonian air and physical exertion can cause dehydration faster than expected. Check weather forecasts at the ranger station for the next 2-3 days.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Las Torres area westward along the W Trek toward the Valle del Francés. The trail passes through open steppe and lenga beech forest with views of Lago Nordenskjöld shimmering below. This section is approximately 11km to Camping Italiano, taking 4-5 hours at a comfortable pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: FEATURED EXPERIENCE — Valle del Francés Day Trek: Drop your heavy pack at Camping Italiano (free camping area) and begin the spectacular Valle del Francés ascent. This glacially carved valley is flanked by hanging glaciers on the Paine Grande massif and dramatic granite spires including Fortaleza and Espada peaks.
day_by_day.evening: Continue up the valley to Mirador Británico if energy allows — the highest viewpoint on the W Trek with 360-degree views of the entire massif. Descend back to Camping Italiano before dark (remember: sunset is around 22:00). Set up camp and rest.

meals.breakfast: Early camp breakfast — instant oatmeal, energy bars, and coffee before the long trekking day
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten on the trail or at the bottom of Valle del Francés — sandwiches and snacks
meals.dinner: Camp dinner at Camping Italiano — pasta with olive oil and tuna, hot soup

day_by_day.notes: Camping Italiano is a free CONAF campsite with basic facilities (no hot showers). Leave your heavy pack here and do the Valle del Francés with a daypack only. Listen for the thunderous crack of calving glaciers and ice falls — a truly unforgettable sound. The hanging glaciers are best viewed in morning light.

day_by_day.morning: Continue the W Trek westward from Camping Italiano toward Paine Grande Lodge area. The trail hugs the northern shore of Lago Nordenskjöld and later Lago Skottsberg with stunning turquoise glacial waters. This section is approximately 9km taking 3-4 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Paine Grande area near the shores of Lago Pehoé. Optional short hike to the viewpoint above the lodge for panoramic views of Lago Pehoé, the Grey Glacier tongue, and the western face of the Paine massif bathed in afternoon light.
day_by_day.evening: Camp at Camping Paine Grande (approx. USD 12-18 per person). This is one of the most scenic campsites in the park with direct views of the mountains reflecting in the lake. Celebrate the halfway point of your W Trek with a slightly more elaborate camp meal.

meals.breakfast: Camp breakfast before packing up — oatmeal with honey and nuts
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the trail with views of Lago Nordenskjöld
meals.dinner: Camp dinner — rice with dehydrated vegetables and soy sauce, hot chocolate and biscuits for dessert

day_by_day.notes: The catamaran from Lago Pehoé to Puerto Natales is available here if needed as an emergency exit from the park. Winds on this section of the trail can be extremely strong — afternoon winds regularly exceed 80km/h in December. Secure your tent carefully with all available guy ropes and stakes.

day_by_day.morning: Day hike to Mirador Grey: Trek from Camping Paine Grande northward along the western arm of the W Trek toward Lago Grey and the Grey Glacier. The trail winds through ancient lenga beech forest with icebergs visible in the lake. Total hike to Mirador Grey: approximately 11km one way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Reach Mirador Grey for stunning close-up views of the 6km-wide Grey Glacier calving into the lake. Watch electric blue icebergs floating silently on the turquoise water — one of the most surreal natural spectacles in South America. Take time to absorb the scale and silence of the glacier.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Camping Paine Grande for your second night. Rest and prepare gear for the return journey tomorrow. The long summer evening provides perfect golden hour photography light on the mountains across the lake.

meals.breakfast: Early camp breakfast — instant oatmeal, energy bars, and hot coffee
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Mirador Grey with glacier views — the best lunch spot in Patagonia
meals.dinner: Camp dinner — bean and vegetable stew with bread, herbal tea

day_by_day.notes: Do not attempt to walk on or near the glacier ice without a certified guide — the ice is extremely dangerous with hidden crevasses. Budget glacier trekking tours are available from Paine Grande Lodge but cost USD 50-80 per person. The free hike to the mirador offers spectacular views without the cost.

day_by_day.morning: Break camp at Paine Grande and take the CONAF catamaran across Lago Pehoé to the eastern park area (approx. USD 25-30, runs 09:00 and 12:00 in high season — book in advance). This 30-minute boat ride offers spectacular views of the entire Paine massif from the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at the eastern catamaran dock and hike or take a park bus to the Salto Grande waterfall — a powerful cascade connecting Lago Nordenskjöld and Lago Pehoé. Short, easy 30-minute loop trail with dramatic rushing water and mountain views. Continue to Mirador Cuernos for views of the iconic Cuernos del Paine peaks.
day_by_day.evening: Arrange transport back to Puerto Natales by late afternoon bus (departs around 17:00-18:00, approx. USD 10-15). Arrive Puerto Natales in the evening. Check back into Aegean Bliss Resort, take a long hot shower, and enjoy a well-deserved restaurant meal.

meals.breakfast: Final camp breakfast before departure — everything left in the food bag
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or snacks on the catamaran and during afternoon hikes
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a sit-down restaurant dinner in Puerto Natales — La Mesita Grande for wood-fired pizza (USD 12-16) or Afrigonia for a local set menu

day_by_day.notes: Book the catamaran in advance online or at the Paine Grande Lodge reception — it fills up quickly in high season. This is your last night in the park area so take time to reflect on the incredible landscapes you have experienced. Wash and dry all gear tonight for the remaining days.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Eve in Puerto Natales. Rest and recovery day after the multi-day trek. Sleep in, do laundry, and recharge at Aegean Bliss Resort. Visit the local artisan market near the waterfront for handmade Patagonian souvenirs — wool goods, leather items, and local crafts at reasonable prices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a free self-guided walk along the Costanera waterfront promenade to Mirador Dorotea trailhead. Optional budget hike up Cerro Dorotea (3-4 hours return, free) for panoramic views of Puerto Natales, Última Esperanza Sound, and the distant peaks of Torres del Paine on the horizon.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve dinner in Puerto Natales. Many local restaurants offer special holiday menus. Explore the town's festive atmosphere with Chilean families celebrating Nochebuena (Christmas Eve) — the main celebration in Chilean tradition.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local café — fresh medialunas (croissants), coffee, and juice
meals.lunch: Local almuerzo set menu — typically the best value meal of the day in Chilean restaurants (USD 6-9)
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve special — treat yourself to a nicer meal at El Living or Última Esperanza restaurant (USD 15-20) — a justified splurge after completing the W Trek

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve (Nochebuena) is the main Chilean Christmas celebration — expect restaurants to be busy and some shops to close early. Book dinner reservations in advance. The Cerro Dorotea hike is underrated and crowd-free compared to the national park trails.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Day. Take the morning bus back to Torres del Paine National Park for a final day visit (departs Puerto Natales around 07:30). Visit the less-crowded southern sector of the park — Lago del Toro area and the Laguna Verde circuit for quiet, crowd-free Patagonian scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Laguna Azul sector in the northeastern park — a stunning turquoise lake backed by the Torres peaks with far fewer trekkers than the main W Trek routes. Hike the 2-hour circuit around the lake shore for reflections of the towers in the calm water.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Puerto Natales on the afternoon bus (departs park around 17:00-18:00). Final evening at Aegean Bliss Resort. Pack for departure and organize any remaining souvenirs. Reflect on 12 incredible days in one of the world's most spectacular landscapes.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before bus departure — bread, eggs, and coffee
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch at Laguna Azul — cheese, crackers, fruit, and chocolate in a stunning natural setting
meals.dinner: Final Puerto Natales dinner — Patagonian lamb (cordero) is the regional specialty and worth trying at least once. El Asador Patagónico offers excellent value lamb dishes (USD 15-18)

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Day means reduced bus schedules — confirm times the day before. Laguna Azul is one of the most beautiful and least-visited spots in the park — a perfect final memory. Carry your park entry pass from Day 3 as it is typically valid for multiple days within the same trip.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Patagonia. Wake early and take one last walk along the Puerto Natales waterfront at sunrise — the mountains of the Andes glow pink and gold in the morning light over Última Esperanza Sound. Visit a local café for a farewell breakfast and pick up any last-minute souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time, arrange shared shuttle transfer from Puerto Natales to Punta Arenas airport (approx. USD 10-15, 3-hour journey). Depart Puerto Natales with memories of one of the most spectacular wilderness adventures on Earth.
day_by_day.evening: Airport departure procedures at Punta Arenas. If flight departs late, explore Punta Arenas city center — the Cementerio Municipal (free, extraordinary) and Plaza Muñoz Gamero are worth a brief visit. Farewell to Patagonia.

meals.breakfast: Final Patagonian breakfast at a local café — café con leche and fresh pastries
meals.lunch: Airport or packed lunch for the journey
meals.dinner: Airport meal or onboard flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3.5-4 hours total travel time from Puerto Natales to Punta Arenas airport including check-in. Book your shuttle in advance as they fill up quickly. Total estimated budget for 12 days excluding flights: USD 400-600 per person covering park entry, campsites, food, transport, and activities — achievable with careful planning and self-catering on the trail.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Punta Arenas or Puerto Natales airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort in Torres del Paine. Check in, unpack, and get oriented with the resort facilities. Rest and prepare for the days ahead.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — travel day
meals.lunch: Not applicable — travel day
meals.dinner: Light snack or late-night bite at the resort's bar or in-room dining if available. Keep it simple after a long travel day.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your transfer to the resort in advance. Pack a light carry-on snack for the journey. The resort is approximately 1.5–2.5 hours from Puerto Natales depending on road conditions. Set an early alarm for Day 2.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in to recover from travel. After a leisurely breakfast, take a gentle orientation walk around the resort grounds and nearby lakeshore. Familiarize yourself with the surrounding landscape, spot local birdlife such as condors and flamingos, and take in your first views of the Paine Massif.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Torres del Paine National Park visitor center to pick up maps, learn about trail conditions, and purchase your park entrance pass. Take a short introductory walk along the Lago del Toro shoreline trail — a flat, scenic 2–3 km stroll perfect for acclimatization.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a relaxed evening. Attend any orientation briefing offered by the resort about upcoming hikes and park regulations. Watch the long Patagonian sunset (often past 10 PM in December) from the resort terrace.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the resort restaurant — fuel up with eggs, local bread, fresh fruit, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at the resort or a nearby park café. Try a Chilean cazuela (hearty meat and vegetable soup) or empanadas.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort restaurant. Order grilled Patagonian lamb (cordero al palo) or fresh trout. Mid-range wine from the Maipo or Colchagua Valley pairs beautifully.

day_by_day.notes: Park entrance fees for foreigners are approximately USD $35–$45 per person in peak season. Keep your receipt as it is valid for multiple entries during your stay. Drink plenty of water to acclimatize.

day_by_day.morning: Puma and Wildlife Tracking Safari — Join an expert naturalist guide at dawn (depart resort around 6:00 AM) for a wildlife tracking experience across the pampas and hillsides surrounding the park. Search for pumas, guanacos, Andean condors, foxes, and rheas in their natural habitat. This is one of the best wildlife experiences in Patagonia.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort by midday. Rest, have lunch, and spend the afternoon reviewing your gear and packing for the upcoming W Trek segment. Visit the resort's gear shop or reception to rent any missing trekking equipment such as trekking poles or gaiters.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the resort. Review trail maps and logistics for the W Trek starting tomorrow. Early bedtime recommended.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast or packed snack provided by the resort before the safari departure at 6:00 AM.
meals.lunch: Hot lunch back at the resort after the safari — try a hearty lentil stew or a sandwich with local cheese.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort. Try pasta with Patagonian lamb ragù or a vegetarian quinoa bowl. Keep the meal nourishing but not too heavy before the trek.

day_by_day.notes: The wildlife safari typically lasts 4–6 hours. Bring binoculars, a camera with a zoom lens, warm layers, and sun protection. Puma sightings are not guaranteed but are increasingly common in Torres del Paine. December light is excellent for photography.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek Day 1 — Begin the iconic W Trek. Transfer to the Laguna Amarga entrance and hike toward Refugio Las Torres. The trail winds through lenga beech forest and open steppe with dramatic views of the Torres granite spires ahead. Distance: approximately 9 km, 3–4 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue settling into Refugio Las Torres. Drop your pack, explore the immediate surroundings, and rest your legs. Take a short walk to the nearby river viewpoint in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner and overnight at Refugio Las Torres (Mountain Lodges of Patagonia or EcoCamp-style refugio, mid-range option). Share stories with fellow trekkers. Prepare gear for the sunrise hike tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before transfer, or packed breakfast to eat en route.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the trail — sandwiches, energy bars, dried fruit, and nuts prepared by the resort or purchased the day before.
meals.dinner: Set dinner at Refugio Las Torres — typically a three-course meal including soup, a main of pasta or meat, and dessert. Included with most refugio bookings.

day_by_day.notes: Book refugio accommodations well in advance — Torres del Paine fills up months ahead in peak season (December–February). Carry a 3-liter water capacity and water purification tablets. Weather can change rapidly; pack all layers in your daypack.

day_by_day.morning: Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike — Wake at 4:00 AM and begin the steep ascent to the base of the iconic three granite towers before sunrise. The final boulder-field scramble leads to the glacial tarn reflecting the towers in golden morning light. This is the most photographed view in all of Patagonia. Round trip: approximately 8 km, 4–5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend back to Refugio Las Torres, have a late brunch, and rest. In the afternoon, hike or transfer toward Refugio Los Cuernos along the shores of Lago Nordenskjöld. Distance: approximately 11 km, 3–4 hours of scenic lakeside walking.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Refugio Los Cuernos. Shower, stretch, and enjoy the stunning views of Los Cuernos del Paine reflected in the lake at golden hour.

meals.breakfast: Very early snack before sunrise hike — energy bar, banana, and thermos of hot coffee or tea.
meals.lunch: Late brunch back at the refugio after descending — eggs, toast, and soup.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Refugio Los Cuernos — hearty set menu with local flavors. Enjoy a glass of Chilean carménère.

day_by_day.notes: The sunrise hike is the highlight of most visitors' entire Patagonia trip. Start no later than 4:30 AM to catch first light. Headlamps are essential. The boulder scramble at the top requires careful footing — trekking poles are highly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek Day 3 — Valle del Francés Day Trek. From Refugio Los Cuernos, hike into the spectacular Valle del Francés — a glacially carved valley flanked by hanging glaciers, soaring granite walls, and the thunderous sound of ice calving. Ascend to the Mirador Británico viewpoint for panoramic views of the entire massif. Distance: approximately 14–16 km round trip, 6–7 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue hiking through the valley, pausing at viewpoints to watch for condors soaring overhead and listen for avalanches on the surrounding glaciers. The afternoon light on the hanging glaciers is extraordinary in December.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Refugio Los Cuernos or hike on to Refugio Paine Grande (approximately 10 km further west along the lake). Overnight at Refugio Paine Grande.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Refugio Los Cuernos before the long day hike.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at the Mirador Británico — sandwiches, trail mix, chocolate, and fruit.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Refugio Paine Grande — set menu. Celebrate the halfway point of the W Trek.

day_by_day.notes: Valle del Francés is one of the most dramatic sections of the W Trek. The round trip to Mirador Británico is long — start early and keep a steady pace. Wind in the valley can be intense; secure all loose items. This is a full and physically demanding day.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek Day 4 — Grey Glacier section. Hike from Refugio Paine Grande westward toward Lago Grey and the Grey Glacier. The trail offers increasingly dramatic views of the glacier's blue ice face and floating icebergs on the lake. Distance: approximately 11 km one way, 4–5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition — Arrive at the glacier zone and embark on a guided kayaking expedition through iceberg-dotted waters alongside the massive Grey Glacier. Paddle close to towering ice formations and learn about glacial dynamics from your guide. This is a once-in-a-lifetime experience.
day_by_day.evening: Overnight at Refugio Grey, located right at the edge of the glacier lake. Watch the sunset paint the ice blue and pink from the refugio deck.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Refugio Paine Grande before departure.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the trail or a light snack at the kayaking staging area.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Refugio Grey — warm up with hot soup and a hearty main course after a cold kayaking afternoon.

day_by_day.notes: The Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition must be booked well in advance and typically costs USD $80–$130 per person. Waterproof gear and dry bags are provided but bring a warm base layer. Water temperature is near freezing — safety briefing is mandatory.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek Day 5 — Final leg and exit. Hike back from Refugio Grey toward Refugio Paine Grande (approximately 11 km). Take your time on the return, revisiting views you may have rushed past on the way in. Catch the catamaran or ferry across Lago Pehoé from Paine Grande back toward the park exit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer back to Aegean Bliss Resort. Arrive mid to late afternoon. Check back in, enjoy a hot shower, and decompress after 5 days on the trail. Take a gentle walk around the resort grounds to stretch your legs.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory dinner at the resort restaurant to mark the completion of the W Trek. Treat yourself to a special meal and a bottle of Chilean sparkling wine (Espumante).

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at Refugio Grey before the hike out.
meals.lunch: Snack on the catamaran or a quick bite at the Paine Grande dock café.
meals.dinner: Full celebratory dinner at the resort — splurge slightly with Patagonian lamb, local seafood, or a tasting menu if available. You've earned it.

day_by_day.notes: Check catamaran schedules in advance — the Lago Pehoé crossing runs at limited times and must be reserved. The alternative is hiking the full circuit back, adding 3–4 hours. Confirm your resort reservation was held during your W Trek days.

day_by_day.morning: Full rest and recovery morning. Sleep in, enjoy a long breakfast, and take a gentle yoga stretch or foam rolling session on the resort terrace. Your body has just completed one of the world's great treks — honor that with rest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the resort's surroundings on a casual, flat nature walk along the lakeshore or nearby estancia trails. Bring your binoculars for birdwatching — look for black-necked swans, flamingos, and Magellanic woodpeckers. No elevation gain, no rush.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a nearby hot spring or the resort's spa facilities if available. Enjoy a massage or soak to soothe tired muscles. Light dinner and early evening.

meals.breakfast: Extended leisurely breakfast at the resort — order everything on the menu if you like. You've earned the calories.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort café — fresh salad, local cheese board, and a cold Austral beer.
meals.dinner: Casual dinner at the resort or a nearby local restaurant in Puerto Natales if a day trip is possible. Try a traditional Chilean parrilla (mixed grill) or cazuela.

day_by_day.notes: This is a mandatory rest day — do not underestimate post-trek fatigue. Hydrate aggressively, eat well, and let your joints recover. Use this time to charge all devices, organize photos, and do laundry if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Puerto Natales — the charming gateway town to Torres del Paine. Browse the local artisan market for Patagonian wool goods, leather crafts, and handmade jewelry. Visit the Museo Histórico Municipal to learn about the region's indigenous Kawésqar people and early settlers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the Seno Última Esperanza (Last Hope Sound) waterfront promenade. Visit Cueva del Milodón Natural Monument (approximately 24 km from Puerto Natales) — a massive cave where a giant prehistoric ground sloth (mylodon) once lived, with dramatic landscape views.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve dinner in Puerto Natales. Join the local festive atmosphere — many restaurants offer special Christmas Eve menus. Return to the resort for a quiet, reflective evening under the Patagonian stars.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before departing for Puerto Natales.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a mid-range restaurant in Puerto Natales. Try Afrigonia (fusion Patagonian-African cuisine) or El Living for excellent food and atmosphere.
meals.dinner: Special Christmas Eve dinner — book in advance at a Puerto Natales restaurant or return to the resort for their holiday menu. Try king crab (centolla) if available — a Patagonian delicacy.

day_by_day.notes: Puerto Natales is approximately 1.5–2.5 hours from the park depending on your resort's exact location. Rent a car or book a private transfer for the day. Cueva del Milodón entrance fee is approximately USD $10. Reserve Christmas Eve dinner well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Day — Sunrise photography walk near the resort. December 25 in Patagonia offers spectacular long-day light. Hike to a nearby viewpoint for golden hour photography of the Paine Massif. Bring your camera and a thermos of hot coffee for a magical Christmas morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional half-day guided horseback riding excursion through the Patagonian steppe — many estancias near the park offer this experience. Alternatively, take a scenic drive along Route Y-290 through the park for wildlife spotting from the vehicle (guanacos, foxes, condors, and possibly pumas).
day_by_day.evening: Christmas dinner at the resort — enjoy whatever special holiday menu the resort has prepared. Share the table with fellow travelers and celebrate the season in one of the most remote and beautiful places on Earth.

meals.breakfast: Special Christmas breakfast at the resort — enjoy the full spread with local pastries, fresh juice, and hot drinks.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch in the field during the horseback ride or vehicle tour — sandwiches, fruit, and local snacks.
meals.dinner: Christmas dinner at the resort restaurant — expect a festive multi-course menu with Patagonian specialties. Toast with Chilean sparkling wine or pisco sour.

day_by_day.notes: Horseback riding excursions typically cost USD $60–$100 per person for a half-day. Book through the resort or a local operator. December 25 is a public holiday in Chile — some services may be limited, so plan ahead. Enjoy the magic of a Patagonian Christmas.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Torres del Paine. Wake up early for one last sunrise over the Paine Massif from the resort terrace. Pack your bags and take a final short walk to your favorite viewpoint near the resort. Reflect on the incredible experiences of the past 12 days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Transfer to Punta Arenas airport or Puerto Natales for your onward journey. If time allows before transfer, stop at a local shop in Puerto Natales to pick up final souvenirs — Patagonian wool, local jams, or a bottle of Chilean wine.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Patagonia. If your flight is in the evening, enjoy a final dinner at the Punta Arenas airport area or a nearby restaurant. Carry the memories of Torres del Paine with you as you head home.

meals.breakfast: Final full breakfast at the resort — savor every bite.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Puerto Natales or at a restaurant near the airport. Try a final empanada or a bowl of caldillo de congrio (Chilean fish chowder).
meals.dinner: Airport area dinner in Punta Arenas if time permits — try Sotito's Bar or La Luna restaurant for excellent Patagonian seafood and a proper farewell meal.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3–4 hours for the resort-to-airport transfer. Confirm your flight departure time and transfer timing the night before. Punta Arenas airport has limited facilities — arrive early. Consider shipping any oversized souvenirs or extra gear home to avoid baggage fees.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Torres del Paine, Patagonia Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Torres del Paine, Patagonia

experiences.name: W Trek Multi-Day Hike
experiences.description: Embark on the iconic W Trek, a 4-5 day trekking route through Torres del Paine National Park covering the Valle del Francés, Grey Glacier, and the iconic Torres lookout. Experience dramatic landscapes of granite towers, turquoise lakes, and diverse Patagonian wildlife including guanacos and condors.
experiences.location: Torres del Paine National Park, Central Circuit

experiences.name: Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Trek to the base of the iconic three granite towers at sunrise for the most photographed view in Patagonia. The 8-hour round trip hike ascends through lenga beech forests and a steep moraine to reveal the breathtaking turquoise lagoon reflecting the towering peaks in golden morning light.
experiences.location: Sector Las Torres, Eastern Torres del Paine

experiences.name: Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition
experiences.description: Paddle through iceberg-dotted waters alongside the massive Grey Glacier, one of Patagonia's most spectacular ice fields. Guided kayaking tours bring you up close to towering blue ice walls and calving glaciers while navigating the pristine waters of Lago Grey surrounded by raw Patagonian wilderness.
experiences.location: Lago Grey, Western Torres del Paine

experiences.name: Valle del Francés Day Trek
experiences.description: Hike through the dramatic Valle del Francés, a glacially carved valley flanked by hanging glaciers, waterfalls, and the towering Paine Grande massif. The trail winds through native Patagonian forest to Mirador Británico, offering panoramic views of the central massif and surrounding peaks with frequent condor sightings overhead.
experiences.location: Valle del Francés, Central Torres del Paine

experiences.name: Puma and Wildlife Tracking Safari
experiences.description: Join an expert naturalist guide for a dawn wildlife tracking experience in the pampas and hillsides of Torres del Paine, one of the best places on Earth to spot wild pumas in their natural habitat. The guided 4x4 and on-foot excursion also offers sightings of guanacos, Andean foxes, rheas, and condors across the sweeping Patagonian steppe.
experiences.location: Laguna Amarga and Pampas Zone, Northern Torres del Paine

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Punta Arenas or Puerto Natales airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged by Aegean Bliss Resort awaits at arrivals. Settle into your Beachfront suite, enjoy a welcome amenity — chilled Carménère, local charcuterie board, and artisan chocolates prepared by the resort. Brief orientation with your dedicated concierge regarding the 12-day program.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: In-suite welcome dining experience: curated cold cuts, Patagonian cheeses, smoked lamb empanadas, and a bottle of premium Chilean wine arranged by the resort

day_by_day.notes: Flight UA lands 22:30. Ensure resort is notified of flight number for real-time tracking. Pack trekking gear in carry-on for easy access. Hydrate well upon arrival — Patagonian altitude and dry air can be dehydrating.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late start — resort orientation breakfast followed by a guided introduction walk around the resort grounds and beachfront. Meet your dedicated private naturalist guide who will accompany you throughout the trip. Review the full 12-day itinerary and gear check session.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scenic private drive into Torres del Paine National Park for an introductory acclimatization hike along the Laguna Amarga entrance trail. Gentle 2-3 hour walk through lenga beech forest with views of the Paine Massif. Spot Patagonian wildlife including guanacos, Andean condors, and ñandú (rheas). Return to resort by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the beachfront terrace — pisco sours and local craft beers with panoramic views of the lake and mountains. Gala welcome dinner at the resort's signature restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the resort restaurant — freshly baked medialunas, smoked Patagonian trout, farm eggs cooked to order, fresh fruit, and premium coffee selection
meals.lunch: Elegant picnic prepared by the resort chef, enjoyed at a scenic lakeside viewpoint during the acclimatization hike — quinoa salad, artisan sandwiches, local cheeses, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Signature welcome dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort restaurant — slow-roasted Patagonian lamb (cordero al palo), king crab bisque, and a curated wine pairing from a boutique Chilean winery

day_by_day.notes: This is an acclimatization day — do not overexert. Drink plenty of water. Sunscreen and UV-rated sunglasses are essential even on cloudy days. Wind in Patagonia can be extreme; always carry a windproof shell jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Early rise for the Puma and Wildlife Tracking Safari — depart at 05:30 with an expert naturalist guide into the pampas and hillsides surrounding the park. Golden hour light creates spectacular photography conditions. Track puma footprints, observe guanaco herds, Andean foxes, and with luck, spot a puma in its natural habitat. This is a world-class wildlife experience unique to Patagonia.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to resort by 10:00 for a late gourmet brunch. Afternoon at leisure — enjoy the resort's spa facilities, heated pool, or simply relax on the beachfront terrace. Optional: private fly-fishing session on a nearby Patagonian river arranged through the resort's concierge.
day_by_day.evening: Private stargazing experience on the resort beachfront with a resident astronomer. Torres del Paine's remote location offers some of the Southern Hemisphere's clearest night skies. Enjoy warm mate tea and wool blankets provided by the resort during the session.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn energy breakfast before safari — thermos of premium coffee, energy bars, fresh fruit, and warm facturas (pastries) prepared by the resort kitchen
meals.lunch: Late gourmet brunch at the resort — avocado toast with Patagonian smoked salmon, eggs Benedict, fresh juices, and a Bloody Mary bar
meals.dinner: Intimate dinner at the resort's private chef's table — a 5-course tasting menu featuring seasonal Patagonian ingredients, including centolla (king crab), Magellanic lamb, and native berry desserts with paired wines

day_by_day.notes: Safari departure is 05:30 sharp — set multiple alarms. Wear muted earth-tone clothing to avoid startling wildlife. Binoculars are essential; the resort can provide high-quality pairs. Photography guides are available upon request.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the W Trek Multi-Day Hike — Day 1 of 4. Private luxury van transfer to the Lago Grey sector. Start trekking the western arm of the W toward Grey Glacier. The trail winds through native lenga beech and ñirre forests with stunning views of turquoise Lago Grey dotted with floating icebergs. Approximately 11 km hike to Refugio Grey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue hiking along the Grey Glacier viewpoint trail for close-up views of the 6 km-wide glacier face. Marvel at the deep blue crevasses and towering ice seracs. Arrive at premium glamping or refugio accommodation pre-arranged by the resort concierge with private room upgrades.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset views over Grey Glacier from the refugio terrace. Hot shower, warm meal, and a well-earned rest. Socialize with fellow trekkers or enjoy a quiet evening journaling with views of the glacier.

meals.breakfast: Power breakfast at the resort before departure — steel-cut oats, protein-rich eggs, smoked meats, and freshly pressed juices
meals.lunch: Gourmet trail lunch pack prepared by the resort chef — hearty wraps, energy balls, dried fruits, nuts, dark chocolate, and electrolyte drinks
meals.dinner: Dinner at Refugio Grey — hearty Patagonian stew, fresh bread, and wine; premium upgrade arranged by concierge for private dining setting

day_by_day.notes: Pack the night before: 3 liters of water, trekking poles, waterproof jacket, gaiters, and a warm mid-layer. The W Trek requires moderate-to-high fitness. Trail distance today: ~11 km. Elevation gain: ~300m. Weather can change rapidly — always be prepared for rain, wind, and sun within the same hour.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek Day 2 — Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition. Rise early for a world-class kayaking adventure on Lago Grey. Paddle through iceberg-strewn waters alongside the massive Grey Glacier with a certified guide. Witness the glacier's scale from water level — an utterly humbling and unforgettable experience. Dry suits and all safety equipment provided.
day_by_day.afternoon: Post-kayak hot lunch at Refugio Grey. Begin the return trek eastward from Grey sector toward Paine Grande, the central hub of the W Trek. Approximately 9 km hike through open pampa with sweeping views of the Paine Massif. Check into Paine Grande Lodge with premium room upgrade.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the spectacular evening light on the Cuernos del Paine (Horns of Paine) from the lodge deck. Optional massage or physiotherapy session available at the lodge to ease trekking muscles. Early rest in preparation for tomorrow's demanding Valle del Francés hike.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Refugio Grey — porridge, eggs, toast, and hot beverages before kayaking
meals.lunch: Hot post-kayak lunch at Refugio Grey — pasta with Bolognese sauce, salad, fresh bread, and hot chocolate
meals.dinner: Dinner at Paine Grande Lodge — grilled trout, roasted vegetables, and a glass of Carménère from a premium Maipo Valley vineyard

day_by_day.notes: Kayaking requires a brief safety briefing and fitting of dry suits — allow 30 minutes before launch. No prior kayaking experience needed. Total trekking distance today: ~9 km. Keep electronics in waterproof bags during kayaking. Glacier calving can occur without warning — maintain safe distance as instructed by guide.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek Day 3 — Valle del Francés Day Trek. Depart Paine Grande at 07:00 for the crown jewel of the W Trek. Hike up the spectacular glacially carved Valle del Francés, flanked by hanging glaciers, soaring granite spires, and the thunderous sound of ice avalanches. Ascend to Mirador Británico for panoramic 360-degree views of the entire Paine Massif.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend Valle del Francés and continue east along the W toward Campamento Italiano and Los Cuernos. Arrive at luxury accommodation at Hotel Las Torres or equivalent premium lodge pre-booked by the resort. Rest and recovery with hot showers and a restorative afternoon tea.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset photography session guided by your naturalist guide at a curated viewpoint near Los Cuernos. The alpenglow on the Cuernos del Paine at sunset is among the most dramatic natural light shows in the world. Return to lodge for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early packed breakfast at Paine Grande — energy bars, fruit, yogurt, and thermos coffee consumed on the trail
meals.lunch: Gourmet trail lunch in Valle del Francés — enjoyed at Mirador Británico with views of hanging glaciers: artisan sandwiches, fruit, nuts, and premium energy snacks
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at the lodge restaurant — 4-course meal featuring Patagonian lamb chops, truffle risotto, and a decadent chocolate fondant with native calafate berry coulis

day_by_day.notes: Valle del Francés is the most demanding section of the W Trek. Round trip to Mirador Británico is approximately 14 km with 600m elevation gain. Trekking poles are strongly recommended. Watch and listen for ice avalanches from the hanging glaciers — a breathtaking natural spectacle. Helmets are not required but remain on marked trails.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek Day 4 — Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike. The most iconic experience in all of Patagonia. Depart at 04:30 in darkness to reach the base of the Torres del Paine granite towers at sunrise. The 8.5 km ascent through lenga beech forest and glacial moraine culminates at a turquoise lake reflecting the three towering granite spires bathed in golden dawn light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from Mirador Las Torres and return to Hotel Las Torres for a triumphant late breakfast. Transfer back to Aegean Bliss Resort via private luxury vehicle. Afternoon at leisure — spa, pool, or beachfront relaxation. Celebrate completing the W Trek.
day_by_day.evening: Special W Trek completion celebration dinner at the resort — private dining setup on the beachfront terrace with candles, premium wine, and a personalized menu curated by the head chef in your honor.

meals.breakfast: Pre-hike 04:00 breakfast — thermos of strong coffee, energy bars, and warm pastries; full celebratory brunch upon return to Hotel Las Torres: eggs, smoked meats, pastries, and fresh juices
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort upon return — Patagonian seafood chowder, fresh bread, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Private beachfront W Trek completion dinner — 6-course chef's tasting menu with champagne toast, centolla king crab, Patagonian lamb, and a wine flight from premium Chilean and Argentine vineyards

day_by_day.notes: Alarm at 03:45 for 04:30 departure — this is non-negotiable for sunrise timing. Headlamps are essential. The final 45-minute scramble over moraine boulders requires careful footing in the dark. The sunrise at Las Torres is one of the most extraordinary sights in the natural world — this effort is absolutely worth it. Temperature at the towers can be near freezing at dawn even in December.

day_by_day.morning: Full rest and recovery day. Enjoy a leisurely sleep-in followed by a long, indulgent breakfast at the resort. Morning spa treatment — book a deep tissue massage, hot stone therapy, or Patagonian botanical body wrap to restore trekking-weary muscles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided photography tour in the resort surroundings — your naturalist guide leads a gentle 2-hour lakeside walk focused on landscape and wildlife photography techniques. Capture the Paine Massif reflections on the lake, guanacos grazing, and Andean condors soaring overhead. Afternoon tea on the terrace upon return.
day_by_day.evening: Private wine and cheese tasting hosted by the resort sommelier — explore a curated selection of Patagonian and broader Chilean wines paired with local artisan cheeses, Magellanic smoked meats, and native preserves. Learn about the unique terroir of southern Chilean viticulture.

meals.breakfast: Extended late breakfast at the resort — full à la carte menu, freshly squeezed juices, artisan coffee, and a Patagonian fruit platter featuring calafate berries, maqui, and rosa mosqueta
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch — grilled fish tacos, ceviche, fresh salads, and sparkling lemonade
meals.dinner: Casual elegant dinner at the resort — wood-fired Patagonian lamb asado, roasted root vegetables, chimichurri, and a bottle of premium Malbec from Mendoza

day_by_day.notes: This is an intentional rest day after 4 days of demanding trekking. Physiotherapy or sports massage is highly recommended — ask the concierge to arrange. Stay hydrated and eat well to aid muscle recovery. Gentle movement is better than complete inactivity for recovery.

day_by_day.morning: Private day excursion to Cueva del Milodón Natural Monument — a 30-minute drive from the resort. Explore the enormous prehistoric cave where remains of the giant ground sloth (Milodón) were discovered. Private expert guide provides a fascinating geological and paleontological narrative. Walk the surrounding nature trails through native forest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scenic drive and stop at Mirador Cerro Castillo for panoramic views of the Torres del Paine massif from the exterior. Continue to Puerto Natales for a curated private cultural tour — visit the local artisan market for authentic Patagonian crafts, hand-knitted wools, and native art. Enjoy a private visit to a local estancia (ranch) for a behind-the-scenes look at traditional Patagonian sheep farming.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort. Private sunset horse-riding session along the beachfront and surrounding pampa — a quintessentially Patagonian experience arranged by the resort's concierge. Gentle ride suitable for all experience levels.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast — smoked salmon bagels, avocado, poached eggs, fresh fruit, and premium coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a top-rated Puerto Natales restaurant — Ultima Esperanza or equivalent premium local restaurant featuring fresh king crab, local seafood, and Patagonian craft beer
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort — grilled Patagonian beef tenderloin, truffle mashed potatoes, roasted asparagus, and a premium Argentine Cabernet Sauvignon

day_by_day.notes: Cueva del Milodón is a UNESCO-listed site — photography is permitted but treat the space with respect. Puerto Natales artisan market is best visited in the afternoon when most vendors are open. Horse riding experience requires closed-toe shoes; riding helmets are provided.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Eve special experience — private dawn hot air balloon flight over Torres del Paine National Park (subject to weather and wind conditions; resort concierge will confirm 24 hours prior). Float silently above the Paine Massif, glaciers, and lakes as the morning sun illuminates the landscape in extraordinary golden light. Champagne toast upon landing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to resort for a festive Christmas Eve brunch. Afternoon at leisure — enjoy the resort's heated infinity pool overlooking the lake, beachfront hammocks, or a second spa treatment. Optional: private guided kayaking on the resort's lake with mountain backdrop.
day_by_day.evening: Gala Christmas Eve dinner at the resort — a spectacular festive feast with live Patagonian folk music, traditional Chilean holiday dishes, premium wines, and a midnight toast. Dress code: smart casual. The resort will have special holiday decorations and a warm, celebratory atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Champagne and light pastries served after the hot air balloon landing — a celebratory post-flight breakfast in the field
meals.lunch: Festive Christmas Eve brunch at the resort — a lavish spread of seafood, carved meats, salads, holiday pastries, and sparkling wine
meals.dinner: Gala Christmas Eve dinner — 7-course festive menu: centolla king crab cocktail, Patagonian lamb rack, Christmas pudding, and a premium Champagne and wine pairing; live traditional Chilean music

day_by_day.notes: Hot air balloon flights are entirely weather-dependent — the resort will arrange an equally spectacular alternative (private helicopter scenic flight) if conditions are unsuitable. Christmas Eve in Patagonia falls in midsummer — expect long daylight hours until 22:00+. Smart casual attire recommended for the gala dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Day — private guided Puma and Wildlife Tracking Safari repeat session at dawn for those who wish to try again or experience different terrain. Alternatively, enjoy a completely leisurely Christmas morning with breakfast in bed service, resort spa, and beachfront relaxation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided boat excursion on Lago del Toro or Lago Pehoé — cruise through the stunning glacial lake with views of the Cuernos del Paine and Paine Grande. Your naturalist guide narrates the geology, ecology, and history of the region. Stop at a scenic island for a Christmas Day picnic.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Day sunset cocktail hour on the beachfront — the resort arranges a special holiday cocktail menu featuring Patagonian pisco creations and local craft spirits. Christmas dinner at the resort's finest table with personalized menu and holiday wine selection.

meals.breakfast: Christmas breakfast in bed or at the resort — festive spread with smoked salmon, eggs royale, holiday pastries, fresh fruit, and premium Champagne or sparkling juice
meals.lunch: Christmas Day picnic on the glacial lake island — gourmet hamper prepared by the resort chef: lobster rolls, truffle deviled eggs, artisan cheeses, fresh fruit, and chilled Chardonnay
meals.dinner: Christmas Day dinner at the resort — roasted Patagonian lamb leg, glazed root vegetables, cranberry and calafate berry sauce, Christmas pudding flambé, and a premium Burgundy wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Day in Patagonia is a public holiday — some external services may be limited, but the resort is fully operational with enhanced holiday staffing. The 21-hour daylight at this latitude means Christmas 'evening' will still be brilliantly sunny — sunglasses required at dinner on the terrace.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Patagonia — rise early for one last solo sunrise walk along the resort beachfront to absorb the landscape in quiet reflection. Enjoy a long, indulgent farewell breakfast at the resort. Final packing and luggage preparation. Concierge arranges gift-wrapping of any artisan purchases made during the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Farewell scenic drive through Torres del Paine National Park with your private naturalist guide — a final loop past key viewpoints including Lago Sarmiento, Laguna Amarga, and the iconic Torres silhouette. Say goodbye to the guanacos, condors, and the extraordinary landscape that has defined this journey.
day_by_day.evening: Private luxury transfer to Punta Arenas or Puerto Natales airport for departure. The resort provides a premium farewell hamper for the journey — Patagonian wines, artisan chocolates, dried calafate berries, and a handwritten farewell note from the resort team. Depart with memories of one of the world's most extraordinary destinations.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the resort — full à la carte menu, every item on offer, with a complimentary glass of Champagne to toast the journey
meals.lunch: Elegant farewell lunch at the resort or en route — Patagonian seafood platter, fresh ceviche, and a final glass of Chilean white wine
meals.dinner: Farewell hamper for the journey — premium Patagonian snacks, wines, and artisan treats for the airport and flight

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure transfer time with the concierge the evening before — allow at least 3 hours for the drive to Punta Arenas airport. Export restrictions apply to some food items; check Chilean customs regulations for items in the farewell hamper. Consider purchasing a bottle of premium Carménère or Malbec from the resort wine shop as a lasting memento. This concludes your 12-day premium Patagonia experience.
